title: No growth of device, host, Python-object or cache footprint across 150 repeated forward+backward+Adam iterations of every differentiable path

fixture.loop: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True); result = model(parameters); loss = objective(result); loss.backward(); optimizer.step(); the parameters are clamped back into the path's contract (epsilon >= 1, passive oscillators); result and loss are deleted; every tenth iteration torch.cuda.synchronize(), gc.collect() twice and the sample is taken
fixture.optimizer: torch.optim.Adam, lr 1e-3, on every trainable input of the path so the autograd graph and optimizer state are those of a real design loop

paths.differentiable_cuda_fused: DifferentiableSimulation, 2D 40 x 30 cells, 60 steps, float32 on CUDA, AdjointOptions(checkpoints=3, backward_kernel='fused'); parameter epsilon (Nx,Ny,Nz)
paths.plane_cuda: DifferentiablePlaneSimulation on the same grid with two x-normal FieldMonitors, two frequencies, block_size 8; parameter epsilon
paths.reversible_cuda: ReversibleSimulation, all-periodic 3D 12^3 cells, 40 steps, float32 on CUDA (fused forward, fused adjoint); parameter epsilon
paths.dispersive_cuda: DispersiveSimulation on the 2D grid with two poles, AdjointOptions(checkpoints=2); parameters epsilon_inf, strength, omega0, gamma
paths.tensor_project_cuda: tensor_from_project (TensorProject: TensorDielectricSimulation with the fixed isotropic CPML collar), 3D 16^3 cells (3 CPML layers, the tensor block inside the interior collar), 40 steps, float32 on CUDA, checkpoints 2; parameter the [materials, 6] tensor table
paths.streamed_host_banks_cuda: StreamedSimulation on the 2D grid, StreamedAdjointOptions(device='cuda', slab_width=8, temporal_depth=4, checkpoints=2, state_storage='host'); parameter epsilon on the CPU
paths.source_waveform_cuda: SourceWaveformSimulation on the 2D grid with two soft sources, AdjointOptions(checkpoints=3); parameters epsilon and the waveform table

fixture.device_memory_bound: every fixture stays far below 1.5 GB of device memory; the driver refuses to start if less than 2 GB is free

measures: CuPy default device pool used_bytes and total_bytes when CuPy is importable
process RSS and private bytes (psutil memory_info on Windows)
live torch tensors: objects in gc.get_objects() whose type has torch.Tensor in its MRO
captured CUDA graphs: torch.cuda.CUDAGraph objects in gc.get_objects()

module caches: cuda_kernels._compile, injection._incident_line, streamed_cost.replay_blocks and streamed_work._replay_summary cache_info().currsize; cuda_bootstrap._module presence; capabilities.RULES and LANES lengths; batch._WORKER_CANCEL presence; live PlaneReferenceCache instances and their tensor_bytes
live instances of the solver's own state holders: _System (and subclasses), _Checkpoints, FusedYeeCUDA, FusedAdjointCUDA, SlabBlockOperator, TileWorkspace, StateStore
growth: for every measure, growth = max over the samples taken after the warm-up (iterations 30 to 150) minus the value at the warm-up sample (iteration 20); a negative growth is reported as measured

acceptance.torch_reserved_note: one large-pool segment of the CUDA caching allocator (20 MiB); the small pool grows by 2 MiB segments, so any growth above zero is reported and anything above one large segment fails
acceptance.cupy_pool_note: CuPy's pool rounds allocations to 512-byte units and keeps freed chunks; 2 MiB is the allowance for one late first-touch chunk
acceptance.verdict: a path passes only if every measure satisfies its limit; a failing path is a leak to be traced to the reference that keeps tensors alive and fixed with a regression test

notes: Python's object count and RSS fluctuate by allocator bookkeeping; the 100-object and 2 MiB allowances cover that noise, not a real per-iteration retention. A lru_cache whose currsize reaches its maxsize is bounded, not leaking; the register-level statement of every module-level container is in docs/ADJOINT_LEAK_SOAK.md.
